items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I‟ve got some very interesting color slides and they presented very well, the color maintained. We‟ve got slides that are very precious, Sammy Davis dancing with Sinatra on the piano with Basie playing the piano.

ctx.x: One thing we didn‟t talk about to the extent that I should have is your photo collection. How many photos do you have?

We have over 70,000 photos, indexed and cross-indexed so anywhere… anybody that we‟d take… musicians, these are musicians. We call it… and I put a thing on it and come up with a number and then pull it right out. And my young friend David, [unintelligible] he‟s very responsible for that sort of stuff. We haven‟t even begun the color. I‟ve got lots of color but we haven‟t filed the color. I‟ve got some very interesting color slides and they presented very well, the color maintained. We‟ve got slides that are very…

Well in terms of having someone do that, documenting and putting into category all of the color photos, might be something that someone working for the Smithsonian or some person who‟s looking to get a degree or something like that, working with the Smithsonian, might be interested in doing.

items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: So Frank called us. So naturally we were going to do it for the Chairman of the Board.

ctx.x: I’ll tell you one of the most poignant appearances I ever made with Benny Goodman. It was during the Reagan administration at the White House. And the King of Jordan was coming to a state visit. And usually when a dignitary would come they’d ask you what kind of music does he like, and he could decide if he liked opera, they’d get an opera singer, if he likes jazz, they’ll get a jazz singer. So the King of Jordan says well I’d like, I’m interested in jazz. So the Chairman of the Board was musical administrator…

likes jazz music.” Benny says, “Okay, you call.” So Frank called us. So naturally we were going to do it for the Chairman of the Board. So we get to the White House and now Benny wants a rehearsal. And you know Buddy Rich ain’t going to make no rehearsal. But of course I was there at the rehearsal, Bucky was there, and Hank Jones and I were there, up in Benny’s apartment and we come up there and sit around for a half hour, and Benny comes up, “Hello fellas.” He picks up his horn. He says, “Thank you I’ll see you…
